newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi prince takes off into airline industry.
newsitem.headline: Saudi prince takes off into airline industry.

text.p: From his palace in Riyadh or his yacht in Nice, Saudi Arabia's Prince al-Waleed bin Talal has conquered the world of banks, hotels, chain stores, and theme parks. Now he is taking off into the airline industry.
The billionaire nephew of Saudi Arabia's King Fahd said on Wednesday he had purchased five percent of stock in Trans World Airlines for investment purposes.
"I have a big portfolio and this is part of diversification," the prince told Reuters by telephone from his Riyadh office. He would not elaborate on his latest acquisition.

Financial analysts close to the prince said the purchase fell within the prince's business strategy of buying stakes in ailing companies and trying to put them back on their feet. TWA on Tuesday announced wider than expected net losses.
The prince's TWA stake is not as big as his other global investments, but his office in Riyadh said his latest buy -- the first in the airline industry -- was a new investment trend.
The analysts said the trend might also include bankrupt Dutch plane maker Fokker for which the prince has been touted as a possible saviour.
Prince al-Waleed -- who turned 40 on March 7 -- is a grandson of Saudi Arabia's founder Ibn Saud.
People who know him say he started with a relatively small amount of money from his father and is now one of the wealthiest and most powerful business moguls in the oil-rich kingdom.

Surrounded by a close circle of advisors, he controls an international portfolio that includes a bank, an investment firm, a supermarket chain, a broadcasting operation, and huge property holdings including the Fairmont and Four Seasons hotel chains.

He has helped bail out the Euro Disney theme park near Paris and Canary Wharf in London's Docklands. He also bought stakes of former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's television and advertising business Mediaset.
Earlier this year he bought Paris' luxury George V hotel.

In a most unlikely scenario for a prince from a conservative Moslem country, Prince Al-Waleed last year signed a deal with U.S. popstar Michael Jackson setting up Kingdom Entertainment to cooperate on concerts, films, television, fun parks and hotels.
His holding company is called Kingdom Establishment. People who know him say he is never far from the telephone even when he goes to the desert or the Mediterranean.
"I've got a rule of thumb: Anything that's worth $4 billion and costs $1 billion -- buy it!" he once said.
The prince is the chairman of the United Saudi Commercial Bank, one of Saudi Arabia's smaller banks which turned into one of its most dynamic when he took over in 1988.
He first showed his Midas touch in 1991 when he bought 14.88 percent of U.S. banking giant Citicorp at a bargain-basement price of about $800 million.
The deal made him the largest shareholder of the United States' largest bank. He also invested $100 million in upmarket retailer Saks Fifth Avenue.
Earlier this month he said he was building a commercial complex in Riyadh, to house a Four Seasons Hotel, for $500 million, dubbed the largest commercial building in the region.
The prince is a 1979 graduate in sciences from California's Menlo Park College. He also received a master's degree in social science at the University of Syracuse. Prince al-Waleed has two children.
The prince and his teenage daughter escaped with light injuries when they had a car crash in Riyadh earlier this year.
